title: Language Model-Driven Kernel Discovery for High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization
claim: Prompting an LLM with raw observations fails once inputs grow high-dimensional; our approach searches a broader space of effective candidates beyond base compositions.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line; left stacked low/high-dim prompts, right kernel-space blobs
description: The figure has two halves separated by a vertical dashed line. On the left, two stacked boxes show LLM-based Bayesian optimization. The top, green box is low-dimensional BO. A short prompt with example points goes into an LLM block and produces a recommendation labeled 'Improvement', marked 'Under Context Limit'. The bottom, red box is high-dimensional BO. The prompt is long with many numbers, and the LLM replies that patterns are hard to extract. The result is 'No Improvement', marked 'Out of Context Limit'. Red highlights draw the eye. On the right, a gray 'Valid Kernel Space' holds a small purple circle of blue base kernels and red designed kernels. Dashed blobs grow across iterations 1, 2, T-1 and T, with green discovered kernels. An orange glow marks 'Effective Kernels for HDBO'.
caption: Motivation Figure. (Left): In high-dimensional BO, a conventional LLM-based BO does not work due to the out-of-context limits and the difficulty of extracting meaningful patterns. (Right): Our pipeline enables us to discover effective kernels for high-dimensional BO beyond compositions.
abstract: Gaussian Process (GP) kernels are central to Bayesian optimization (BO), yet designing effective kernels for high-dimensional problems still relies on extensive manual engineering. Existing automated approaches struggle in high dimensions for two bottlenecks: their kernel search space is limited to additions and multiplications of base kernels, and Large Language Model (LLM)-based approaches require conditioning on raw observations, which becomes infeasible due to context-length limits and the difficulty of extracting meaningful patterns. We introduce Kernel Discovery , an LLM-driven evolutionary framework for high-dimensional BO that searches a broader kernel space beyond predefined composition rules and does not require conditioning on observations. Motivated by the observation that directly prompting an LLM to generate kernel code yields syntactically varied but functionally identical kernels, we adopt a two-stage approach: an LLM first proposes novel mathematical forms, then a second LLM call converts each form into validated, executable code. We also utilize LOO-CRPS instead of MLL as a selection criterion to penalize overfitted kernels. On five high-dimensional BO benchmarks, our method achieves an average rank of 1.0 out of 17 , outperforming competitive baselines. We further analyze the discovered kernels to identify which kernels lead to improvements in high-dimensional BO.
